# Results — Study 781 (Quad-Witching-Hangover)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **the
week after quad-witching underperforms**: the market is left "hungover" after the quarterly
four-way expiration churn. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month). Fingerprint `a7fba5aedc7e` (SPY, adjusted/total-return daily
closes, one tape).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, `SPY` (S&P 500 ETF), one tape: 5,555 rows, 2004-06-01 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 84 quad-witching Fridays 2005→2025, third Friday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec (CBOE/CME quarterly expiration calendar) |
| Events resolvable | all **84** of 84 quad-witching Fridays have SPY coverage around the anchor |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of SPY's raw forward return across independent, non-overlapping quarterly events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo per cut; leave-one-out jackknife |
| Execution / costs | **calendar-known, zero look-ahead**: quad-witching is the third Friday of the quarter's last month, fixed years ahead. Hangover = [anchor → anchor+K]; run-in = [anchor−K → anchor]; net of 2× one-way cost × NAV. Gross AND net reported |
| Price basis | **total-return** (dividends reinvested, `auto_adjust=True`) |

**Self-benchmarked, named:** SPY *is* the index, so there is no cross-sectional benchmark
leg — the test is on SPY's *own* forward return. SPY drifts up (~+0.03%/session over this
sample), so "underperform" must mean *below that drift*; the random-window placebo cloud
(mean ≈ +0.24% per 5-session window) is exactly that yardstick, and the observed hangover
is compared against it.

## The hangover — SPY raw forward return, K sessions AFTER the quad-witching close

| cut | n | mean | *t* | up-rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-week hangover (k=5) | 84 | **+0.075%** | **+0.276** | 35/84 = 41.7% [31.7%, 52.3%] |
| 2-week give-back (k=10) | 84 | +0.375% | +0.937 | 53/84 = 63.1% [52.4%, 72.6%] |

The folklore is **flatly wrong on the sign**: the week *after* quad-witching returns
**+0.08%** on average (*t* = +0.28) — mildly *positive*, not a hangover. (The up-rate is
below half, 41.7%, i.e. slightly more down-weeks than up-weeks, but the positive weeks are
larger, so the *mean* is positive and the *t* is a rounding error.) Stretch to two weeks
and it is more positive still (+0.38%). There is no underperformance to find.

## The run-in (contrast) — SPY return, K sessions BEFORE the quad-witching close

| cut | n | mean | *t* | up-rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-week run-in (k=5) | 84 | +0.188% | +0.660 | 51/84 = 60.7% [50.0%, 70.5%] |

The run-in is also a wash (+0.19%, *t* = +0.66) — every window around the date is
indistinguishable from SPY's ordinary drift. There is nothing special about the calendar
neighbourhood of quad-witching; the "hangover" is calendar pareidolia.

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws per event, left tail = underperform)

| cut | tail | observed | placebo mean (sd) | p |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-week hangover | left | +0.075% | +0.239% (0.256%) | 0.248 |
| 2-week give-back | left | +0.375% | +0.475% (0.346%) | 0.364 |

Both cuts sit **squarely inside** the luck cloud (left-tail p = 0.25 and 0.36) — the
post-quad-witching window is a hair *below* the average random window but nowhere near its
left tail. Ordinary tracking noise, fully.

## Jackknife (leave-one-out) — 1-week hangover *t*

Full-sample *t* = **+0.276**; across all 84 leave-one-out draws the *t* stays in
**[−0.226, +0.592]** — hovering around zero no matter which quarter you drop. There is no
hidden effect masked by an outlier and none created by one.

## Tradability — net of costs (calendar-known entry, zero look-ahead)

| window | gross | net @ 5 bps | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-week hangover | +0.075% (*t* +0.28) | −0.025% (*t* −0.09) | −0.125% (*t* −0.46) |
| 2-week give-back | +0.375% (*t* +0.94) | +0.275% (*t* +0.69) | +0.175% (*t* +0.44) |

To "trade the hangover" you would **short** a window whose gross return is *positive*
(+0.08%): you lose money before costs and more after. Round-trip costs alone flip the
1-week leg negative. There is no edge in any direction — long or short, gross or net.

## Synthetic positive control (deterministic, no network)

- **Null (dip = 0), 20 seeds:** mean *t* = +0.67 (sd 0.93); |*t*| ≥ 2 in **3/20** seeds —
  the small positive mean is the synthetic world's built-in +drift leaking into a
  self-benchmarked one-sample *t* (the same drift SPY has), and the false-positive rate is
  controlled.
- **Planted hangover −0.6% (seed 793):** mean +0.04%, *t* = **+0.16** (drift partly offsets
  a small dip).
- **Planted hangover −1.2% (seed 793):** mean −0.56%, *t* = **−2.19** — a real dip is
  recovered monotonically and turns the detector clearly negative. The machinery works; the
  real tape simply has no dip to recover.

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal — is the effect real?** | **None** | The week after quad-witching returns **+0.08%** (*t* = +0.28), *positive*, not a hangover; the 2-week window is +0.38% (*t* = +0.94); placebo left-tail p = 0.25 / 0.36 (dead centre); jackknife *t* pinned to zero (−0.23…+0.59). Indistinguishable from noise, and the sign is opposite the folklore. |
| **Tradability — survives costs/scale?** | **Mirage** | Nothing to bank. "Shorting the hangover" shorts a *positive* window and loses gross; costs make the 1-week leg negative outright. No edge long or short. |

**In one sentence:** the "quad-witching hangover" is a myth — SPY's week after quarterly
quad-witching is mildly *positive* (+0.08%, *t* = +0.28), sits dead-centre of the
random-window placebo, and offers no tradable edge in either direction.
